why:
phase-417 W4.d — a RE-MAP, not an addition. rclrs expresses throttling as a PARAMETER on one macro -- `log_info!(logger, throttle = Duration, "..")` via `LogParams`/`ToLogParams` -- where we ship a separate macro per severity. Same capability, decomposed differently: a parameter list needs named arguments the macro would have to parse off an arbitrary prefix, and a distinct name is what makes the throttled path resolvable at expansion.

The clock-reading form; without `nros-log/platform-clock` it is a `compile_error!` rather than a throttle that silently admits everything, and `*_throttle_at` takes the caller's timestamp instead.

phase-428 W5 (2026-09-06) — ledgering a recorded sweep finding. W4 F14, and the cluster SPLITS — the recorded finding treated all twelve macros as one preference and they are not. RFC-0036 forbids recording a PREFERENCE as a divergence, so this row says which it is rather than leaving the reader to infer it.

UPSTREAM: rclrs ships six log macros (`log`, `log_debug`, `log_info`, `log_warn`, `log_error`, `log_fatal`) and throttles with a PARAMETER — `log_info!(logger.throttle(d), "..")` via `LogParams` / `ToLogParams` / `ThrottleClock`.

THE SIX BASE `nros_*_throttle!` MACROS ARE A PREFERENCE. A macro per severity where upstream has a modifier is a decomposition choice; the reason recorded above ("a parameter list needs named arguments the macro would have to parse off an arbitrary prefix") is an implementation convenience, not a platform constraint, and `divergence` under RFC-0036 needs the latter.

THE SIX `_throttle_at!` MACROS ARE CONSTRAINED, and that half of the verdict holds. Without `nros-log/platform-clock`, `__nros_throttle_now!` (`packages/core/nros-log/src/macros.rs`) is a hard `compile_error!` — "without a clock `__timestamp_ns()` is a constant 0, so the window would admit every record while looking exactly like a working throttle" — so the caller-supplied-time form is the ONLY throttle available on a clockless target. That is clause 1 doing its job. Their doc also anchors to rclcpp's `RCLCPP_*_THROTTLE(logger, clock, ...)`, not to rclrs.

HOW A USER FINDS OUT: COMPILE ERROR — a ported `log_info!(logger.throttle(d), ..)` names an identifier that does not resolve here. Loud, so the user is not harmed; the defect being recorded is that the ROW claims a constraint for the base six that only the `_at` six have. No disposition is written: which decomposition survives is the phase-417 stage-6 rename decision. Re-verified by hand against the current worktree before this row was written.
